scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being too hard on my boyfriend or if he's overreacting. Let me start by laying out the situation as I see it. First, my partner works full-time from 7 am to 7 pm. That's a long day, and I can imagine he's pretty tired by the time he gets home. I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9 am to 12 pm. We don't live together, but we're local, so we're always in and out of each other's homes. My son, who is 12 years old, decided he wanted to play football on weekends. He's really excited about it, and I think that's great for him. Initially, I was going to ask my boyfriend if he could pay for it, but when I mentioned it to my mom during a visit, she strongly expected me to pay and told me it was my responsibility, not my boyfriend's. Even though he's been in my life for three years, she made it clear that I should handle it. So, I ended up having to pay for it myself. To afford it, I extended my work hours to 9 am to 5 pm. Now, I asked my boyfriend if he could pick up and drop off my son on weekends because, obviously, I'm at work. He looked uncomfortable and said, "Sorry, no can do. This is your dad's responsibility." I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in South London, whereas we live in North London, and his dad doesn't drive, but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did, he wouldn't mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad could take him, but what would be a one-hour-plus journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my boyfriend. He got really angry and told me that he had to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games, etc., since I wasn't home anyway. He said he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quickly. He then suggested that we break up because I was putting too many responsibilities on him. I was like, "Really? Over a bloody football game?" I felt like he was being unreasonable. The little sneak then went over to see my mom, and they had a heart-to-heart, which ended up in her calling me and telling me I was out of line. Now, I'm confused. Who is in the wrong here? Am I being too demanding, or is he overreacting? I think I need to consider a few things here. First, the responsibility of paying for my son's football. My mom made it clear that it's my responsibility, but I'm in a relationship, so shouldn't we share these responsibilities? Or is it reasonable for her to expect me to handle it alone? Second, the request for my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my son. He's already working long hours, and I'm asking him to take on additional responsibilities during his weekends. Is that fair? Or should I be more understanding of his need to relax and have his own time? Third, the argument that led to him suggesting a breakup. Was that an overreaction on his part, or was I being too demanding? How should we handle conflicts like this? I also need to think about the bigger picture of our relationship. Are there underlying issues that this situation has brought to light? Is there a lack of communication or mutual understanding? How can we address these issues to strengthen our relationship instead of letting them lead to a breakup? Maybe I should also consider the role of my mom in this situation. She told me I was out of line, but I feel like she's biased because she's my mom and wants to protect me. How do I balance her advice with my own judgment in this relationship? Overall, I'm feeling a bit lost and unsure of how to proceed. I need to figure out where I stand, what my expectations are, and how to communicate them effectively to my boyfriend without making him feel overwhelmed. I also need to understand his perspective better and see if there's a middle ground where both of us can feel respected and valued in the relationship.
